name: Porter stemmer
notes: Classic 1980 suffix-stripping algorithm. Fast, deterministic, no dictionary. Over-stems some forms (e.g. 'university'->'univers'). Prefer Snowball/Porter2 for new work; kept for parity with legacy indexes.

name: Snowball (Porter2) stemmer
notes: Successor to Porter; the estate DEFAULT prose stemmer. Multilingual, well-maintained, better recall/precision balance than Porter, far less aggressive than Lancaster. Pair with a domain vocabulary for terminology-heavy corpora.

name: Lancaster (Paice/Husk) stemmer
notes: Very aggressive iterative stemmer; smallest index but heavy over-stemming that collapses distinct terms. Use only for high-recall coarse clustering, never for terminology-sensitive domains (health/legal/finance).

name: Krovetz (KStem) stemmer
notes: LIGHT dictionary-backed stemmer: inflectional only, produces real words, minimal over-stemming. Good where readable tokens matter (glossary terms, mixed code+prose) or where Snowball over-stems.

name: spaCy lemmatizer
notes: POS-aware rule+lookup lemmatizer producing dictionary lemmas (not stems). Higher precision than stemming for NLP/IE and knowledge extraction; heavier (needs a loaded pipeline). Preferred where downstream is entity/relation extraction rather than bag-of-words retrieval.
license: MIT (spaCy); model data MIT/CC-BY-SA per model

name: Code-identifier tokenizer (camel/snake split)
notes: Splits programming identifiers on camelCase, snake_case, kebab-case, dotted paths and digit boundaries; lowercases; performs NO linguistic stemming. For source, config, workflow and log corpora where token literals (keys, CVE ids, symbols) must be preserved. Use as the code-file tokenizer in EVERY policy, alongside a prose tokenizer for docs.

name: Unicode word tokenizer (UAX-29)
notes: Unicode Text Segmentation (UAX-29) word-boundary tokenizer for natural-language prose (clinical narrative, contracts, filings, docs). The estate DEFAULT prose tokenizer; feed its tokens to a stemmer/lemmatizer and vocabulary. NOT for source code (use tok.code-identifier).

name: No-op / identity normalizer
notes: Identity pass: tokenize only, do not stem or lemmatize. Correct for code/dev-tooling and security detector corpora where stemming would corrupt literals. Pair with tok.code-identifier.

name: SNOMED CT clinical terminology
notes: Controlled clinical terminology for the health domain: normalize surface terms to SNOMED CT concept ids for retrieval/coding. LICENSED — terminology content is NOT vendored here; use only as a pointer. SNOMED CT requires a SNOMED International Affiliate License (free in UMLS member territories such as the US via the NLM UMLS Metathesaurus). Resolve concepts at ingest against a licensed local terminology server; store only concept ids/refs, never redistribute the release files.
license: SNOMED CT Affiliate License (SNOMED International / IHTSDO) — POINTER ONLY, do not vendor

name: MeSH (Medical Subject Headings)
notes: NLM Medical Subject Headings: free biomedical controlled vocabulary/thesaurus. Usable as an open alternative or complement to SNOMED CT for topic/subject normalization. Public domain (U.S. Government work); may be downloaded directly. Still referenced as a pointer here, not vendored, to keep the dataset content-free.

name: UMLS Metathesaurus
notes: Unified Medical Language System Metathesaurus: cross-maps SNOMED CT, MeSH, ICD, RxNorm, LOINC and 200+ source vocabularies to CUIs. The integration point when a health corpus spans multiple terminologies. LICENSED — free of charge but requires a UMLS Metathesaurus License and NLM/UTS account; content is NOT vendored, pointer only.
license: UMLS Metathesaurus License (NLM) — free but license+account required; POINTER ONLY

name: Legal / regulatory controlled term list
notes: Controlled vocabulary for legal/regulatory/compliance corpora, assembled from OPEN public-domain and permissively-licensed sources: eCFR/US-GPO defined terms (public domain), EuroVoc (EU multilingual thesaurus, EUPL), and Cornell LII glossary references. First-party assembled list; no proprietary or client legal content. Normalize surface terms to canonical regulatory concept labels before matching gates/policies.
license: first-party term list; sources public-domain (eCFR/GPO) + EUPL (EuroVoc)

name: Finance / capital-markets controlled term list
notes: Controlled vocabulary for finance/markets corpora, assembled from OPEN sources: the US-GAAP XBRL Financial Reporting Taxonomy (FASB, freely available), SEC EDGAR filing element labels, and public accounting glossaries. First-party assembled list; no vendor/client market data or proprietary marketing materials. Normalize surface terms to canonical reporting concepts for profitability/economic-profit indexing.
license: first-party term list; sources FASB US-GAAP taxonomy (free) + public glossaries
